question: Will exhausted ballots exceed the winning margin in the 2026 US Senate election in Alaska?

calls.reasoning: Four-candidate RCV general: Peltola vs Sullivan with minor candidates Sullivan Jr. (2.5% primary) and Heikes (1.1%). Expected cumulative inactive/exhausted ballots ~8-11k (~2.5-3.5% of turnout) from first-round blanks/overvotes plus ~45-50% exhaustion of minor-candidate votes, consistent with 2024 House (7,595 exhausted). YES needs a final-round margin below ~3 points; October RCV polls show Peltola +2 to +3 (DfP 51-49, InsiderAdvantage 50.1-48, ASR 51-49), and with Alaska polling error SD ~5-6 pts the chance of a margin that small is ~35%. A first-round majority (resolves No) is mostly confined to lopsided outcomes. Historical Alaska statewide RCV races I checked: exhausted > margin in 1 of 3 (2022 special yes; 2022 Senate no; 2024 House no but close). No matching market: Polymarket only prices party winners.

calls.reasoning: Peltola leads Sullivan by about 2 points in the final round in October polling (RCP +2.2; DFP's ranked-choice simulation 51-49). The 2024 House precedent: final margin 7,876; exhausted ballots 7,595 (narrow No); Wikipedia's cumulative 'inactive' count including blanks and overvotes was 14,007 (clear Yes). The question's wording ('cumulative', citing Wikipedia) leans toward the inactive count, weighted about 65%. In 2026 the minor candidates hold about 3.6-5%, so exhausted ballots should be about 2% and the inactive total about 3.5-4% of ballots. Assuming the margin is centred on D+2.5 with a typical miss of 5-6 points, that gives about 0.28 under the exhausted reading and about 0.45 under the inactive reading, blending to about 0.40. Name confusion with Sullivan Jr. could raise exhaustion. No market on this question was found; the harness-listed Polymarket contracts cover party control only.

calls.reasoning: Yes requires (a) no candidate reaching 50% of first choices, otherwise there is no RCV round and it resolves No, and (b) a final margin smaller than cumulative exhausted ballots. Peltola polls about 48-50% first-choice (NYT/Siena 50-43, InsiderAdvantage 48.2-42.6, PPP 48-47), so P(RCV round) is about 0.55-0.6. The minor candidates (Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., Heikes) drew only about 3.6% in the primary, implying roughly 5-8k exhausted ballots (2024 House precedent: 7,595 exhausted vs an 8,354 margin; 2022 Senate: 12,933 inactive incl. blanks vs about 19k margin). Final-round polls put Peltola +2-5 (about 7-16k votes), so P(margin < exhausted | RCV) is about 0.45. Upside risks: name-confusion votes for the second Sullivan, and the resolver counting blanks/overvotes as inactive. No matching human market found; the Polymarket sweep markets only indicate Peltola is favoured.

calls.reference_class: Alaska statewide RCV general elections 2022-2024 (exhausted/inactive ballots vs final-round margin, plus whether tabulation occurred)

calls.reasoning: YES requires (a) no first-round majority, since Alaska skips ranked-choice tabulation otherwise and the fine print then makes it No, and (b) a final margin below exhausted ballots. With minor candidates at ~4.5% and Peltola's two-way share around 51.5% (SD 3.5), P(ranked-choice round) is ~0.46. Given a round, ~46% exhaustion of minor votes (2024 House precedent) gives P(exhausted > margin) of ~0.5. That is ~0.24 overall under an exhausted-only reading and ~0.40 if Wikipedia's cumulative 'inactive' row (with ~1.6% blanks and overvotes) is used. Weighting the inactive reading at ~55% gives ~0.33. The question's own wording and the Wikipedia citation lean toward the inactive row.
calls.reconciliation: Factual check 1: Sullivan Jr. remains on the ballot; ballots are set and early voting has started, so a four-candidate field is certain. Check 2: the official 2024 House RCV report gives final 164,861-156,985 (margin 7,876), exhausted 7,595, blanks 5,788, overvotes 624. Exhausted-only was a narrow No; inactive-including-blanks was a clear Yes. This settles the 2024 numbers in Run 2's favour; Run 3's figures are earlier unofficial ones. Judgment disputes: Run 3 handled the no-ranked-choice-round path correctly (Runs 1 and 2 underweighted it), but it underrated how narrow the margin must be once a round happens. With only ~4.5% minor share, a round implies a first-round margin under ~4.5 points, which makes exhaustion vs margin roughly a coin flip. The resolution definition is ambiguous; I weight the inactive reading ~55% because of the 'cumulative' wording and the Wikipedia citation. My hand-calculated model gives ~0.24 for exhausted-only and ~0.40 for inactive, so ~0.33. No human market matches; the Polymarket contracts are party-sweep combinations only.
